with simplicity i envision an app where i travel and my laptop node controls my home node like a pupped, is sign in with a google or facebook login so my home node knows its me and then it acts like puppet so i can do anything on the road i do at home, a join-like app, generalized can be a panel of options for me to tie my home node into my remote control, by identifying myself to it by and email verification using google facebook sendmail, whatever.

In plain words, the way I hear it: on the road, your laptop node drives your home node as its puppet, and you can do there anything you do at home. The one new piece is how the home node comes to trust the laptop in the first place: you prove it's you through something you already have (a Google or Facebook sign-in, or a code by email), and after that the laptop's key is simply its owner. A generalised join: a panel of ways to tie a node of yours to your remote control.
Two notes so we keep it simple:
- The puppet half exists already: the owner door (a puppet obeys its owner's key) and design/relay/DEVICE.md ('a device is the owner's window'). What's missing is only the sign-in step that binds the laptop's key.
- It's a different goal from app-plugins/G1. By tonight's rule it gets its own session, not items under this one.
Go! = I record it as the next goal to design, parked until G1 closes.

wsl-claude, checking the road idea against your own design: you already drew it, the other way round. design/relay/DEVICE.md (design, not built): 'if a node is the person, a device is a window onto that person and must carry none of them with it'; your words, 'an ejectable UI surface'. By that, the laptop on the road isn't the OWNER of your home node (making home a puppet of the laptop would move 'who you are' onto the laptop, and a lost laptop would own you). It's a DEVICE: a window onto the home node, doing everything you do at home through it, holding no key that is you.
Your 'join-like app, a panel of options' then IS the device pairing step, and Google/Facebook/email is only how the home node recognises you the first time before it accepts the laptop as a window. After that, keys do the work, and ejecting the device (a stolen laptop) is one action at home.
So the simple version is already your design; what's missing is building it. Worth a goal of its own after this one.
